chess.moves-0: A rook slides along its row or column. A bishop slides along a diagonal, so it stays on one colour all game. Neither can pass a piece. Trace the line with your finger before you move.
chess.moves-1: A queen slides along any straight line or diagonal, as far as it's clear: a rook and a bishop in one. A king goes the same ways, one square at a time.
chess.moves-2: A knight moves in an L: two squares one way, then one to the side. It jumps over anything in between, and it always lands on the other colour.
chess.moves-3: A pawn walks one square forward, or two from its starting row, and never back. It takes one square diagonally forward. On the far row it becomes a stronger piece.

maths.ten-0: Find the pair that makes 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6. Fill one number up to 10 from the other, then add what's over. 6 + 7 is 10 + 3.
maths.ten-1: Hop to the next ten, then do the rest. 38 + 5: 2 gets you to 40, with 3 still to go, so 43. Taking away works the same, hopping down to the ten first.
maths.ten-2: Doubling is adding a number to itself. Split it into tens and ones and double each: 43 doubled is 80 + 6. Times 4 is doubling twice.

coding.var-0: A variable is a name holding one number. Set replaces the number, and change adds to it. Say the number out loud after each block I run.
coding.var-1: Count along with me: add one, step, and say the new value each round. The loop ends when the value equals the target exactly, so a count that skips that number keeps going.
coding.var-2: Each time I stand on a flower I can add one to my count. Stop when the count matches what's asked, even if there are more flowers on the map.
coding.var-3: An if can ask about a value: does steps hold 2 yet? Follow the loop round by round, keep the value in your head, and turn only on the round where the answer is yes.
